# 7-Day Lisbon Trip Plan for 2 Adults

A relaxed Lisbon week with museums, viewpoints, and one day trip fits your budget well if you keep lodging central and use public transit. I’m assuming mid-range 3-star-plus hotels with breakfast included, mostly metro/tram/walking, and one full-day excursion.

# Day-by-Day Lisbon Itinerary and Cost Plan

## Trip Cost Snapshot
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/currency-euro.svg
- Trip window: **2026-04-10 to 2026-04-16**
- Travelers: **2 adults**
- Budget: **€2,400 total**
- Recommended pacing: **1 major sight + 1 lighter activity per day**
- Best-fit spend target: **about €2,050–€2,250**, leaving a buffer for snacks, taxis, or upgrades

| Day | Focus | Main Activities | Est. Daily Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Day 1 | Arrival + Baixa/Chiado | Check-in, easy walk through Baixa, Rossio, Chiado, sunset at a viewpoint | €210 |
| Day 2 | Historic Lisbon | Alfama stroll, Lisbon Cathedral area, São Jorge viewpoint, Fado evening | €230 |
| Day 3 | Museums + Belém | Calouste Gulbenkian or Museu Nacional do Azulejo, Belém monuments, riverside walk | €260 |
| Day 4 | Day Trip | Sintra day trip with one palace and one viewpoint | €290 |
| Day 5 | Modern Lisbon | Parque das Nações, Oceanarium or museum, waterfront downtime | €220 |
| Day 6 | Bairro Alto + Viewpoints | Tram/walking day, Miradouros, Time Out Market, relaxed dinner | €240 |
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/83/Lobster%2C_Time_Out_Market_Lisboa_%2850661858143%29.jpg Alt=| Day 6 | Bairro Alto + Viewpoints | Tram/walking day, Miradouros, Time Out Market, relaxed dinner | €240 |, Lisbon, Portugal
| Day 7 | Final morning + departure | Light breakfast, last shopping, airport transfer | €120 |

## 7-Day Itinerary by Day

### Day 1: Easy Arrival and Central Lisbon
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Arrive, check in, rest, and take a short orientation walk if energy allows.
- Afternoon: Explore **Baixa** and **Chiado**, then pause at a café for a slow lunch.
- Evening: Watch sunset from a nearby viewpoint such as **Miradouro de Santa Catarina** or **São Pedro de Alcântara**.
- Food: Keep dinner simple with petiscos and wine in Chiado.

**Estimated cost for 2:** hotel €135, meals €45, transit €10, extras €20 = **€210**

### Day 2: Alfama, Cathedral Area, and Fado
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Start in **Alfama** and visit the area around **Lisbon Cathedral**.
- Afternoon: Continue to **Castelo/São Jorge viewpoint** area for city views and a slow wander.
- Evening: Book a **Fado** dinner or show for one classic Lisbon night.
- Food: Choose a modest Fado venue or a neighborhood tavern to control cost.

**Estimated cost for 2:** hotel €135, meals €55, transit €10, activity €30 = **€230**

### Day 3: Museum Day and Belém
- Morning: Visit **Calouste Gulbenkian Museum** or **Museu Nacional do Azulejo**.
- Afternoon: Head to **Belém** for Jerónimos area, riverside walking, and a pastry stop.
- Evening: Return early for a relaxed dinner near your hotel.
- Food: Budget for pastries and a lighter dinner; Belém is great for a scenic, low-stress afternoon.

**Estimated cost for 2:** hotel €135, meals €55, transit €10, museum/entry €20, snacks €40 = **€260**

### Day 4: Sintra Day Trip
- Morning: Take an early train to **Sintra**.
- Afternoon: Visit **one major palace** and one viewpoint or garden, not more than that.
- Evening: Return to Lisbon for an easy dinner and an early night.
- Food: Pack a snack and keep lunch casual to avoid tourist-area markups.

**Estimated cost for 2:** hotel €135, transit €30, entry €70, meals €55 = **€290**

### Day 5: Modern Lisbon and Waterfront
- Morning: Explore **Parque das Nações** at a slow pace.
- Afternoon: Choose **Oceanarium** or a contemporary museum, then enjoy the riverside.
- Evening: Have a relaxed dinner back in the center.
- Food: This is a good day for a lunch-and-snack strategy rather than a big sit-down meal.

**Estimated cost for 2:** hotel €135, meals €55, transit €10, activity €20 = **€220**

### Day 6: Viewpoints, Tram Streets, and a Flexible Last Full Day
- Morning: Take a scenic tram/walking loop through central neighborhoods.
- Afternoon: Visit 1-2 viewpoints such as **Santa Luzia** and **Portas do Sol**, then browse shops.
- Evening: Dinner in **Bairro Alto** or **Cais do Sodré**, depending on mood.
- Food: Keep this as your “best dinner night” if you want one nicer meal.

**Estimated cost for 2:** hotel €135, meals €70, transit €10, extras €25 = **€240**

### Day 7: Departure Morning
- Morning: Breakfast, final coffee, and a short souvenir stop if time allows.
- Afternoon: Airport transfer and departure.
- Food: Use hotel breakfast and one light snack before leaving.

**Estimated cost for 2:** hotel €135, transit €20, snacks €10 = **€120**

## Budget Fit for the Whole Trip

| Category | Estimated Total |
|---|---:|
| Hotel, 6 nights with breakfast | €810 |
| Meals and drinks | €350–€450 |
| Transit in Lisbon + airport transfers | €80–€120 |
| Museums, viewpoints, Fado, day trip entries | €320–€420 |
| Buffer for extras | €150–€250 |
| **Total** | **€1,710–€2,050** |

This keeps you comfortably under **€2,400**, with room for a better hotel, a nicer Fado dinner, or a premium Sintra visit.

# Best Ways to Lower Spending Without Losing the Experience

## 1) Stay in a walkable central area, but not the most expensive pocket
- Choose **Baixa, Chiado edge, Avenida, or Intendente** instead of the most premium riverfront areas.
- You’ll still be close to viewpoints, transit, and restaurants.
- Savings: **€20–€50 per night** versus top-tier central hotels.

## 2) Keep the day trip to one palace, not a full Sintra “everything” day
- Sintra gets expensive when you stack several paid entries, taxis, and long lunches.
- Pick **one palace + one scenic stop** and use public transit.
- Savings: **€40–€80 total** without losing the trip highlight.

## 3) Use breakfast-included hotels and make lunch the flexible meal
- Breakfast included removes one daily expense immediately.
- For lunch, alternate between cafés, pastries, and casual spots instead of full sit-down meals every day.
- Savings: **€60–€120 over 7 days** for two people.
